Description

Phospholipase C enzymes cleave PI(4,5)P2 into DAG and IP3 in nociceptors. PLCβ is driven by Gq-coupled receptors such as the bradykinin B2 receptor, and PLCγ1 by NGF through its tyrosine kinase receptor TrkA. IP3 releases Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum, which opens ANO1 chloride channels, depolarises the neuron and triggers action potentials. Antibodies against NGF such as tanezumab reduce knee OA pain.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: NGF sensitises nociceptors.

Colour evidence (1)
MoleculeColourWhyEvidenceRefs
The whole blockredNGF sensitises nociceptors
Blocking NGF relieves OA pain in patients (tanezumab trials), and deleting TrkA in NaV1.8 neurons improves OA pain in mice. Tanezumab also brought rapidly progressive OA, which kept it off the market.
